core_obligations: The Picard group and the Kummer sequence (proof lines 11261-11267): writing the curve as the complement of finitely many points in a smooth projective compactification, its Picard group is a quotient of that of the compactification by the classes of the points, so the degree zero part is divisible and the Kummer sequence gives both the degree zero cohomology and the vanishing in degrees at least two.

The first cohomology (proof lines 11267-11302): the group is described as a quotient of the set of triples consisting of a degree zero invertible module on the compactification, a degree zero divisor supported in the removed points and an isomorphism between the n-th tensor power and that divisor; an exact sequence comparing the first cohomology of the compactification with the direct sum of the n-torsion groups of the removed points is displayed, and counting ranks with the companion computation gives the asserted rank.
proof_roadmap: Express the curve as the complement of finitely many points in a smooth projective compactification.
Use the Kummer sequence and divisibility of the Picard group for the degree zero cohomology and for the vanishing in degrees at least two.
Describe the first cohomology by triples and count ranks through the displayed exact sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the etale cohomology of an affine smooth curve over an algebraically closed field with coefficients in the roots of unity: the degree zero group is the roots of unity in the field, the first group is free of rank twice the genus plus the number of removed points minus one, and the higher groups vanish (statement lines 11245-11258). The proof is a complete computation: the curve is expressed as the complement of finitely many points in a compactification and divisibility of the Picard group together with the Kummer sequence gives the degree zero group and the vanishing in degrees at least two (proof lines 11261-11267); the first cohomology is described through triples and a displayed exact sequence comparing it with the compactification and the removed points, whose ranks are then counted (proof lines 11267-11302). The non-formal content is the description by triples and the rank count. The claim is H2: a computation with each input named.
